highlights.head: Method           One-to-one interactions
points: The PIF team interacted with officials from Agriculture, Horticulture, Fisheries, Micro Irrigation, Tourism, Industries, Mines & Geology, Panchayati Raj, Education, Health, Electricity, Housing, Urban Local Bodies, Rural Water Supply & Sanitation, GST, Swarna Gramam & Key Findings Ward Secretariat, and Grama Panchayat to identify sector- wise growth opportunities and development priorities.

Agriculture and tourism emerged as the key growth drivers of East Godavari district, with officials emphasizing investments in infrastructure, value addition, and convergence across departments to accelerate economic growth.
Agriculture remains the backbone of the district economy, with paddy as the dominant crop, followed by tobacco and maize, highlighting opportunities for productivity enhancement and agro-processing.
Fisheries is a high-growth sector, with around 3,500 acres under aquaculture and plans to expand cultivation to increase production, livelihoods, and district GVA.

District Industries & MSMEs highlighted strong potential in agro-based industries, including rice mills, poultry feed, ethanol, cocoa processing, and traditional clusters, while identifying land availability, finance, and infrastructure as key constraints.
Swarna Gramam & Ward Secretariat emphasized the need for reliable socio-economic data, digital infrastructure, capacity building, and technology-enabled service delivery.

Grama Panchayat officials highlighted priorities such as sanitation, drinking water, waste management, revenue mobilisation, and self-sufficient village institutions to strengthen local governance and public services.
4th July – Constituency Profiling (4 Constituencies)

Interactions were held with officials from Mandapeta, Nidadavolu, Rajanagaram, and Anaparthy constituencies to assess their economic potential, sectoral priorities, implementation challenges, and strategies for promoting sustainable and inclusive regional development.

Agriculture emerged as the primary growth driver across all constituencies, with paddy remaining the dominant crop. Officials highlighted opportunities for crop diversification through oil palm, sugarcane, horticulture, fruits, oilseeds, and natural farming, alongside strengthening Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), agro-processing, and post-harvest infrastructure to enhance value addition and farmers' incomes.

The discussions identified strong opportunities in industry and the services sector, including MSMEs, food processing, handicrafts, industrial parks, tourism, eco-tourism, temple tourism, aviation-linked development, and skill development initiatives. These sectors have the potential to generate employment, promote entrepreneurship, and diversify the regional economy.

Officials also highlighted several cross-cutting challenges, including inadequate irrigation and cold-chain infrastructure, limited market access, shortage of technical institutions and skilled manpower, climate-related vulnerabilities, weak institutional coordination, and infrastructure gaps.

Strengthening public infrastructure, improving market linkages, promoting sustainable industries, and enhancing institutional support were identified as key priorities for accelerating constituency-level economic growth.

sessions.format: In Person One on One interaction
sessions.roles: Deputy Director Agriculture; Assistant Director of Horticulture; Joint Director, Animal Husbandry; District Fisheries Officer; Sub-Divisional Forest Officer
coverage: The programme commenced with an introductory meeting with the Chief Planning Officer, Eluru, Mr K Srinivas Rao, during which the Pahlé India Foundation team introduced themselves and outlined the objectives and expected outcomes of the programme. This was followed by a one-on-one interaction with officials from the Primary Sector Departments to gather field-level insights and understand sector-specific opportunities, challenges, and priorities for economic development.

highlights.head: Primary Sector
points: Aquaculture Leadership with Structural Gaps: Eluru ranks first in shrimp exports in Andhra Pradesh with 1.6 lakh acres under aquaculture, yet lacks local seed hatcheries, adequate processing infrastructure, and stable export pricing — making the sector productive but structurally fragile and heavily dependent on external inputs and volatile international markets.

Agriculture challenged by water and soil issues: Paddy dominate cultivation, but drainage failures in low-lying coastal areas, fish tank water contamination, delayed canal releases disrupting Rabi and Kharif seasons, and declining soil carbon due to limited compost availability are seriously constraining agricultural productivity and farmer incomes across the district.

Horticulture's Post-harvest Bottleneck: Despite a strong production base of 1.68 lakh acres of oil palm and full micro- irrigation coverage, the horticulture sector is held back by absent cold storage, underutilised processing capacity, and 70% tenant farming; limiting value addition and farmers' ability to access government schemes.

Animal Husbandry Performing Well but Unevenly: With over 6 lakh buffaloes and strong veterinary infrastructure, most Animal Husbandry KPIs are near or above target — particularly curative treatment at 105%; but sex-sorted semen adoption at just 34.64%, high fodder costs, and staff vacancies remain critical gaps requiring focused intervention.

Forest and Wildlife Under Dual Pressure: Managing 1,914 sq. km across 7 ranges including Papikonda National Park, the Forest Department balances eco-tourism development and mangrove conservation with growing human-wildlife conflict; Indian Gaur frequently damaging crops, demanding stronger compensation mechanisms and preventive measures to protect both biodiversity and farmer livelihoods.

sessions.format: In Person One on One interaction- Two Sessions: Session 1: Secondary Sector; Session 2: Tertiary Sector
sessions.roles: Deputy Executive Engineer, Housing Department; Revenue Officer, Municipal Corporation; Executive Engineer, Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL); Administrative Officer- Zila Parishad; Assistant Director of Industries; Inspector of Factories; Educational Correspondent (Private School, Headmaster, Zila Parishad High School; Assistant Commissioner-GST; District Manager, Tourism; Municipal Commissioner; District Panchayat Officer; Superintendent Engineering, Panchayati Raj
coverage: The morning session was dedicated to the Secondary Sector, covering departments responsible for industrial production, infrastructure, manufacturing, and allied economic activities. The evening session focused on the Tertiary Sector, bringing together officials from departments engaged in service delivery, governance, health, education, tourism, taxation. This two-session format ensured focused and sector-specific discussions, allowing for deeper engagement with departmental challenges, performance indicators, and development priorities relevant to each sector's contribution to the district's overall Gross Value Added.

highlights.head: SECONDARY SECTOR
points: Electricity fluctuations, gas price rises, and the unresolved Kollaru permissions issue prevent existing aqua processing, food processing, ceramic, and feed mill units from reaching full installed capacity.
Despite leading Andhra Pradesh in shrimp exports, Eluru exports predominantly raw produce, allowing value addition GVA to accrue to processors elsewhere rather than within the district.

Oil palm and coconut processing units operate below capacity, coir processing remains unexploited, and cold storage absence prevents conversion of primary agricultural output into higher secondary sector GVA.

Summer load shedding, voltage fluctuations, and cyclone-related outages impose recurring production losses across all industrial categories, directly suppressing secondary sector GVA below installed capacity potential.

Only ₹2.5 lakh approved against ₹7–8 lakh actual construction cost severely limits housing sector activity, suppressing construction-linked GVA from material purchases, labour wages, and contractor employment.
Insufficient local labour supply and high local wage rates force factories to operate below capacity or defer technology investment, compressing net value added and suppressing factory-level GVA.

highlights.head: TERTIARY SECTOR
points: Despite 6–7 lakh monthly tourists, accommodation gaps and poor connectivity convert potential multi-day visitors into same-day transients, leaving enormous tourism GVA unrealised across the district economy.

Staff shortages, excessive centralisation at Assistant Commissioner level, and unrealistic targets reduce return scrutiny and enforcement capacity, creating tax compliance gaps that deprive the state of legitimate revenue.
Shortages of doctors, nurses, and diagnostic facilities mean illness is detected late and treated poorly, imposing disease burden costs that reduce labour productivity and GVA across all sectors.

Administrative overload on teachers, syllabus pressure, girls' safety gaps, and absent centralised curriculum produce unequal outcomes, limiting the workforce quality that drives long-term district GVA growth.
Zilla Parishad, PRED, PHED, and R&B all face staffing and maintenance gaps, collectively producing rural road, water, and lighting deficiencies that raise logistics costs and suppress rural GVA.
Water scarcity, drainage contamination, road encroachments, parking shortages, and weak food safety enforcement collectively raise urban business costs and suppress Eluru's service sector GVA daily.

sessions.format: Online Google Meet with officials
sessions.roles: Constituency Special Officers; Agriculture Officer ; Horticulture Officer; Assistant Director, Animal Husbandry; District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) Officials ; Fisheries Officials
coverage: Online interactions were conducted with constituency and mandal-level officers across four constituencies, organised into four sessions of 1.5 hours each. The discussions were aimed at understanding the sectoral issues, challenges, and development priorities across each constituency as part of the Swarna Andhra 2047 capacity-building exercise.

highlights.head: Kaikaluru Constituency
points: Aquaculture dominates the constituency's economy within the Kolleru lake catchment, but environmental sustainability is at risk; chemical overuse in horticulture and agriculture, combined with untreated aquaculture wastewater discharge into panchayat ponds, threatens long-term soil and water quality and could jeopardise international export market access.

Fish and prawn are currently sold raw with zero local processing, branding, or value addition, leaving significant income potential unrealised. Establishing local processing plants under a regional Kaikaluru/Kolleru/Godavari- Eluru brand could meaningfully strengthen farmer incomes and export competitiveness.

Grey-water management treatment units are urgently needed to reduce pollution from aquaculture and agricultural runoff, while a dedicated water-hyacinth processing unit could convert this invasive species: prevalent in the Kolleru catchment into a usable natural farming input, creating a circular economy opportunity.

A comprehensive constituency-level field consultation covering agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, and infrastructure is required to complete Kaikaluru's economic profile, as existing data is limited primarily to the aquaculture and environmental sustainability dimensions discussed during the Swarna Andhra 2047 exercise.

highlights.head: Eluru Constituency
points: Eluru Municipal Corporation, serving approximately 3 lakh residents, faces a significant water supply and sewerage gap of around 33,000 households in outskirt and recently-merged villages still depend on water tankers. AMRUT 2.0, including a 15 MLD filtration plant and 20 MLD sewage treatment plant, is the planned intervention targeting universal coverage within 1.5 years.

The constituency's economy is anchored by its well-established carpet industry, making it one of the most industrially active constituencies in Eluru District. Emerging opportunities include pearl culture, combined eggs- meat-fish retail outlets, and chitin and chitosan extraction from aquaculture processing waste in Pondi village, where approximately 330 acres are under fish culture.

Hair-based wig and hair-product industries near Dwarakatirumala - utilising locally available temple-tonsure hair as raw material; represent an identified but untapped manufacturing opportunity that could generate non-farm employment, while Tangallamudi's substantial agricultural land offers significant scope for horticulture crop expansion currently unrealised.

Eluru District recorded the highest number of Kisan Drone subsidies sanctioned in Andhra Pradesh; approximately 45 units; reflecting strong agricultural mechanisation momentum. Additional identified opportunities include a floating solar installation on the Tammileru River and tourism infrastructure development around the Galigopuram temple, both currently underdeveloped.

highlights.head: Unguturu Constituency
points: Paddy cultivation dominates at approximately 58,000 acres constituency-wide, yielding around 32,000 metric tonnes per season, with Nidamarru mandal recording significantly higher productivity — 50 to 55 bags per acre — compared to 25 to 30 bags elsewhere. Natural farming is being piloted on 1,100 to 1,200 acres, with progressive paddy-to-horticulture conversion as the Swarna Andhra 2047 goal.

The complete absence of paddy drying floors and storage godowns across the entire constituency is a persistent and unaddressed infrastructure gap, forcing farmers to dry produce along highways. Combined with procurement bottlenecks for the newer 1053 paddy variety, these constraints are directly suppressing farmer income and post- harvest value retention.

Oil palm is the dominant horticulture crop; approximately 9,000 acres across Unguturu and Bhimadole mandals but faces a notable productivity gap relative to Dwarakatirumala, compounded by Ganoderma fungal disease affecting around 15% of plantations and dripper misuse reducing irrigation efficiency. Flower cultivation under shade nets is identified as a high-GVA emerging opportunity.

Bhimadole mandal alone has approximately 10,900 acres under aquaculture, producing around 58,962 metric tonnes of fish and 28,798 metric tonnes of prawns annually. No local processing or cold storage infrastructure exists ; all catch is sold raw while a newly issued Government Order restoring aquaculture power subsidies and potential IoT-enabled monitoring adoption represent key near-term improvement levers.

highlights.head: Denduluru Constituency
points: Agriculture anchors the constituency economy, with approximately 16,000 kharif acres predominantly under paddy, alongside a progressive shift toward oil palm and cocoa; around 9,500 acres under cocoa and 200 acres recently converted from paddy to horticulture along the Eluru Canal command area. Soil and water salinity is constraining further oil palm expansion in several pockets.

Animal husbandry particularly dairy, sheep, and goat rearing — is a significant livelihood source, yet the constituency has no veterinary medicine retail outlet allocated despite high livestock dependence, and DRDA subsidy is not being routed to local livestock units. Organic milk fetching up to ₹200 per litre and desi eggs at ₹25 to 30 represent high-value premium opportunities being underutilised.

Four active Farmer Producer Organisations; one per mandal alongside sanctioned coir and blackgram processing units, SHG-led cocoa processing units, mushroom cultivation, and dehydrated vegetable units represent a meaningful emerging processing and rural enterprise ecosystem that requires consistent support, timely subsidy release, and market linkage to scale effectively.

Aquaculture in Pedapadu mandal covers approximately 11,166 acres, with the Kolleru lake catchment adding further inland fishing capacity. Contract farming with major seed companies including Kaveri, Syngenta, and Nuziveedu Seeds is active, while Ratnala Cheruvu has been identified as a constituency tourism development site with basic visitor infrastructure investment needed.

coverage: Online interactions were conducted with constituency and mandal-level officers across four constituencies, organised into four sessions of 1.5 hours each. The discussions were aimed at understanding the sectoral issues, challenges, and development priorities across each constituency as part of the Swarna Andhra 2047 capacity-building exercise.

highlights.head: Chintalipudi Constituency
points: Agriculture and horticulture dominate the constituency's economy, with oil palm, paddy, cocoa, coconut, and fisheries offering strong opportunities for value addition, mechanisation, and sustainable livelihood enhancement through improved infrastructure and market access.

The primary sector faces persistent constraints, including inadequate processing and storage facilities, irrigation bottlenecks, labour shortages, tenancy issues, flood risks, and limited post-harvest infrastructure, reducing productivity and farmers' incomes.

Officials emphasized expanding agro-processing, natural farming, micro-irrigation, mechanisation, and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) to strengthen agricultural value chains, improve market linkages, and enhance district Gross Value Added (GVA).

Strengthening rural infrastructure, improving departmental coordination, promoting fisheries and allied sectors, and creating employment through value-added industries were identified as key priorities for achieving sustainable growth under the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision.

highlights.head: Nuzvid Constituency
points: Nuzvid has significant potential in agriculture, horticulture, dairy, and allied sectors, with mango, paddy, maize, oil palm, and livestock serving as major drivers of the constituency's rural economy.

Officials highlighted opportunities for expanding processing industries, micro-irrigation, natural farming, mechanisation, and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) to improve productivity, increase value addition, and generate higher farm incomes.

Key challenges include inadequate processing and storage infrastructure, high labour and cultivation costs, tenancy-related issues, limited irrigation facilities, and dependence on government grants, which constrain long-term economic growth.

Developing mango and oil palm processing units, strengthening dairy value chains, improving rural infrastructure, expanding market linkages, and promoting entrepreneurship were identified as strategic priorities to enhance GVA, create employment, and support the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision.

highlights.head: Polavaram Constituency
points: Agriculture and horticulture are the backbone of the constituency, with oil palm, cashew, paddy, cotton, chilli, and blackgram driving the rural economy. Natural farming, mechanisation, and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) offer significant opportunities for increasing productivity and value addition.

Animal husbandry and fisheries provide important livelihood opportunities, but limited processing facilities, weak market linkages, inadequate storage infrastructure, and low value addition continue to restrict income generation and employment potential.

Remote tribal mandals face persistent development challenges, including poor road connectivity, recurrent flooding, inadequate public infrastructure, staff shortages, and heavy dependence on government support for essential services and livelihoods.

Strengthening agro-processing, rural infrastructure, market access, storage facilities, eco-tourism, technical education, and flood- resilient development to improve Gross Value Added (GVA), generate employment, and support the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision.

coverage: The training programme was conducted in two sessions i.e., morning and afternoon. The morning session focused on the Swarna Andhra @2047 Vision, concepts of national income and GDP estimation, strategies for enhancing Gross Value Added (GVA), and the significance of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in evidence-based planning and monitoring. The afternoon session covered the district profile, key findings and inputs received during stakeholder consultations, and discussions on sectoral opportunities and challenges. points: The morning session was graced by the presence of Smt. Vijaya Laxmi, Director, Planning, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Smt. Rohini, Assistant Director, and Mr. Srinivas Rao, Chief Planning Officer, Eluru. Smt. Vijaya Laxmi delivered insightful remarks on the critical importance of measuring GDP at the lowest levels of the economy, emphasizing that granular economic measurement at the constituency and district level is a powerful instrument for achieving inclusive growth across Andhra Pradesh. She elabo- rated on how decentralized economic estimation enables policymakers to identify spatial and sectoral disparities that aggregate state-level data often conceals; allowing more targeted, equitable, and evidence-driven public investment decisions that reach the most underserved communities and economic segments. She also highlighted the systemic challenges that such grassroots economic measurement addresses, including data gaps, planning inefficiencies, and the disconnect between ground-level reali- ties and state-level policy design. Smt. Vijaya Laxmi concluded her address by warmly acknowledging the work being undertaken by the Pahlé India Foundation team.

Dr. Faizan commenced the programme by introducing Pahlé India Foundation and the team. This was followed by a presentation on the Swarna Andhra @2047 Vision by Mr. K. V. Narayana, who discussed the state's long-term development goals and strategic priorities.

Dr. Krishna Reddy delivered a technical session on the concepts and measurement of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), national income, and various strategies for enhancing Gross Value Added (GVA). The morning session concluded with the technical ses- sion.

All the sessions were highly interactive, with participants showing considerable interest in understanding the concepts and their practical applications in GDP estimation and district-level economic planning. To reinforce learning, participants were given three practice exercises on GDP estimation methods, along with an additional exercise demonstrating the apportionment method used for allocating GVA across districts.

The afternoon session focused on the socio-economic profile of Eluru district and the key insights gathered during interactions with district officials. The presentation highlighted sectoral strengths, challenges, and opportunities identified through stake- holder consultations. The session witnessed active participation from district officials and facilitated meaningful discussions, with complex concepts being explained in a simple and accessible manner.
Also, a case study on integrated farming of Paddy and Fish was discussed with the participants.
An exercise sheet was provided to all the participants regarding the calculation of GDO and also, how to allocate GVA between districts and mandals.

The afternoon training sessions covered the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision, concepts of national income and GDP estimation, strategies for enhancing GVA, and the importance of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

points: The training programme commenced with an introduction to Pahlé India Foundation and the project team. This was followed by a session by Dr. Faizan on the Swarna Andhra @2047 Vision, highlighting its key goals, targets, and long-term development aspirations. Subsequently, Ms. Ragini conducted a technical session on the various approaches to GDP estimation and followed with constituency profiles and then discussed sector-specific strategies for enhancing Gross Value Added (GVA).
Dr. Faizan concluded the technical sessions with a presentation on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs.
The schedule was followed in the same manner in both the constituencies.

The programme witnessed active participation from officials throughout the sessions. Participants engaged enthusiastically, raising insightful questions and contributing to meaningful discussions. The interactive nature of the programme ensured that concepts related to economic measurement were explained in a simple manner, thereby enhancing participants' understanding and overall learning experience.

coverage: The programme covered in-person Constituency Capacity Building Training for Avanigadda, Pamarru, and Penamaluru constituencies, with mandal-level officials presenting sector-wise inputs on Agriculture, Horticulture, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and allied departments under the Constituency Vision Action Plan (CVAP). Discussions focused on sectoral strengths, field-level challenges, and priority interventions to support Gross Value Added (GVA) growth. Under the CVAP, priorities include strengthening mechanization, cold storage, aquaculture infrastructure, and inter-departmental coordination to improve farmer incomes and GVA. Officials from Avanigadda, Challapalli, Ghantasala, Koduru, Mopidevi, and Nagayalanka mandals highlighted labour shortages, inadequate storage and post-harvest infrastructure, drainage issues, and limited procurement support in agriculture, with emphasis on strengthening mechanization, irrigation, and storage facilities. Under the CVAP, priorities include strengthening horticulture infrastructure, processing facilities, market linkages, and value addition to enhance productivity, employment, and GVA.

highlights.head: Avanigadda
points: Fishing and aquaculture account for 48.6% of constituency GVA. Officers sought separate estimation for brackish-water aquaculture, inland fisheries and marine catch because their cost and price structures differ.
Key risks include dependence on Tamil Nadu for aqua seed, cyclone and flood exposure, feed-price volatility and the fall in active aquaculture acreage in Nagayalanka from 11,000 to 4,000 acres.
Given zero rail connectivity, cold-chain and export-logistics readiness to be tracked as a primary KPI — essential for converting Fishing & Aquaculture GVA into higher-value processed exports

With 1,617 registered boats and 9,702 active fishermen but no local vessel maintenance/repair infrastructure, future training to prioritise boat servicing and mechanised aquaculture skills alongside marine biology.

highlights.head: Pamarru
points: Livestock, estimated at ₹1,198 crore, is the largest sub-sector. Participants discussed attribution of income from small dairy and poultry households compared with organised FPO-linked production.
With 78.74% of 13,907 holdings classified as marginal, officers emphasised the need for suitable crop-GVA estimation and seasonal KPI adjustment for canal, weather and market-access effects.
Priority interventions include cold-chain and FPO readiness, dairy and seafood processing, tissue-culture support for banana, and improved extension on fertiliser use and drought risk.

coverage: Session on Swarna Andhra @ 2047 vision, constituency profiling, GDP/GVA/GDDP concepts, KPI linkages, strategies for enhancing economic output etc

points: Data Collection (GDDP/GSDP) — With 73.2% of CGVA from services (₹7,545 Cr) — the highest tertiary share in Krishna district — officers discussed how to cleanly apportion output between Trade, Hotels & Restaurants (₹2,844 Cr, the single largest sub-sector), Transport & Storage (₹1,638 Cr) and Real Estate & Dwellings (₹1,137 Cr), particularly for peri-urban households earning across sectors.

Attribution of Cane Output — The KCP Sugar Factory (7,500 TCD, 15 MW cogeneration) links thousands of cane farmers to a single processing unit; participants deliberated how factory-linked cane output should be split between agriculture and manufacturing GVA without double-counting.

Constituency Profiling — Rapid, unplanned urbanisation within the Amaravati Capital Region is converting fertile farmland and straining drainage; officers proposed treating farm-to-plot land conversion as a structural trend indicator in the baseline, so agriculture KPIs are not misread as productivity decline. Micro-irrigation covers only 177 ha of 20,179 ha cultivable land — flagged as a canal-dependency risk pending Krishna Eastern Branch / Ryves Canal modernisation.

Group Discussion Findings — Excessive historical fertilizer use has degraded baseline soil, and a largely landless-tenant farmer base complicates multi-cropping adoption; local FPOs hold no active processing assets, with Vuyyuru's food-processing dryer unit still under construction; KCP Sugar byproducts remain unutilised for high-margin ethanol; acute storage gaps and 75-kg gunny bag shortages persist, with vacant school buildings being converted into storage as an interim fix.

Swarna Andhra Goals — Toward the ₹28,464 Cr (2028-29) and ₹2,97,678 Cr (2047-48) GCDP targets, cold-chain, warehousing and NH-65 / Machilipatnam Port logistics readiness to be tracked as a primary KPI — converting raw paddy, cane, dairy and inland fish (targeted to double from 36,445 MT to 73,323 MT by 2029) into processed output is the highest-return lever.

Capacity Building — Training to prioritise tissue-culture banana and grafted-vegetable propagation, FPO organisation with packaging/processing assets, RAS & cage-culture aquaculture, and urban-services skills (logistics, construction trades) — reflecting the constituency's peri-urban transition and the agro-processing gaps raised in group discussion.

sessions.format: In person training (10.30 am to 5pm)
sessions.roles: Dy. MPDOs (SGSW), Agriculture Officers / MAOs, Horticulture Officer, ASOs, EOs (PR&RD) and Young Professionals — constituted as 4-member Master Trainer teams per mandal
coverage: ●   Swarna Andhra @ 2047 — Macro blueprint targeting 15% annual GSDP growth, zero poverty (P4 model) and structural economic transformation — translated into localized growth priorities for each mandal. ●   GVA / GDDP Methodology — Mechanics of GVA (= Output − Intermediate Consumption) and how state GVA is apportioned to district level using proxy indicators — GST collections, vehicle registrations, Udyam units and electricity usage — rather than direct data collection. ●   Mandal Master Trainer Framework — Mandate for mandal officers to act as clear interpreters, mentors and feedback loops for the next tier of trainings. ●   KPI Tracking Systems and GVA Linkage — The field-operations tier manages 62% of the Swarna Andhra KPI system (198 mandal-level + 199 district-level KPIs); how to identify potential sectors and link sectoral GVA to various indicators along with their data sources ●   Practical Worksheets & Case Study — Step-by-step exercise on crop value (Acreage × Yield × MSP − input costs) and secondary/tertiary weights via local GST and tourism proxies; Kalamkari cluster analysed as a scaling model using GI branding, design archives and common treatment infrastructure.

points: The Krishna District Master Trainers' Training (ToT) was highly interactive and enriching. Below are the key highlights:

highlights.head: Interactive Sessions
points: ● Sessions were highly interactive, with Master Trainers from every mandal team actively engaging with the GVA/GDDP concepts and relating them to their own department's data. ● Officers raised field-level questions and shared practical reporting challenges, turning the training into a genuine two- way exchange rather than a one-way lecture.
● The session on GDP and GVA measurement, and how mandal-level data rolls up into the district number, generated strong interest, particularly among Agriculture and Horticulture officers.

highlights.head: Hands-On Exercises
points: ● Master Trainers worked through a live worksheet estimating Hotel & Restaurant sector GVA using the allocation method — apportioning the sector's value using GST collections and tourist footfall figures as the district-sharing indicators. ● Participants also practised the crop-value worksheet (Acreage × Yield × MSP − input costs) ● Trainers discussed how to explain proxy-indicator based allocation (GST, vehicle registrations, Udyam units, electricity usage) to the next tier of mandal-level trainees in simple terms.

Case Study — Pedana Kalamkari Cluster ● The Pedana Kalamkari hand-painted and block-printed textile cluster was discussed as a scaling model for Krishna district, given its GI (Geographical Indication) recognition and long-established design heritage. ● Officers examined how GI branding, design archives, and common treatment/dyeing infrastructure could be leveraged to strengthen value addition and market linkages for local artisans.

highlights.head: Sectoral Discussions
points: ● Officers explored Krishna district's comparative sectoral strengths, including agriculture, aquaculture, and handloom/textiles, and discussed strategies to leverage these for district growth. ● Discussions focused on strengthening value chains, improving proxy-indicator data quality, and linking mandal-level activities to the district's Swarna Andhra @ 2047 growth targets. ● Participants discussed their role as Master Trainers in cascading these concepts accurately to mandal-level teams in the next round of trainings.

highlights.head: Feedback
points: ● JD (Joint Director) — Good session; better understanding of the concepts. ● AD (Assistant Director) —clearly specify what officers should do with the master training and whom they should train ● General — Concepts were understood despite the sessions being in English; the Telugu translation by the trainer greatly helped in the session ; font size of the slides should be increased; concepts should be related to the KPIs; the session was engaging enough that officers attended the whole day — though they usually find it difficult to sit that long in regular meetings.

sessions.format: One-to-one interactions 2nd – 3rd July – District Profiling › Agriculture & Horticulture: With an average landholding of 2.36 acres, officials emphasized extending institutional credit to tenant farmers (over 75% of cultivators), strengthening crop insurance coverage, and improving support for small and marginal farmers. › Fisheries: The upcoming crab hatchery is expected to drive significant value addition. However, the sector faces challenges such as high feed costs and limited adoption of biofloc technology, highlighting the need for technology support and investment. › Animal Husbandry: The sector reported strong livestock health management and disease-free vaccination coverage, but identified staff shortages as a major constraint to sustaining service delivery and productivity.

highlights.head: Method               One-to-one interactions
points: Agriculture & Horticulture: With an average landholding of 2.36 acres, officials emphasized extending institutional credit to tenant farmers (over 75% of cultivators), strengthening crop insurance coverage, and improving support for small and marginal farmers.

Fisheries: The upcoming crab hatchery is expected to drive significant value addition. However, the sector faces challenges such as high feed costs and limited adoption of biofloc technology, highlighting the need for technology support and investment.

Animal Husbandry: The sector reported strong livestock health management and disease-free vaccination coverage, but identified staff shortages as a major constraint to sustaining service delivery and productivity.

highlights.head: Key Findings
points: Transport: APSRTC highlighted its contribution to inclusive mobility and district GVA through welfare schemes, while prioritizing electric buses, fleet modernization, and EV charging infrastructure to support sustainable growth.

Tourism: Officials identified the district's coastline as a key growth driver, proposing regular beach festivals, tourism circuits, and experiential tourism to increase visitor footfall and local economic activity.

Marketing & Logistics: Officials emphasized market linkages for marginal farmers, expanded cold storage infrastructure, and leveraging Krishna's strong logistics potential to improve value realization, strengthen supply chains, and promote economic growth.
4th July – Constituency Profiling (4 Constituencies) Gannavaram, Gudivada, Pedana and Machilipatnam

Key Development Bottlenecks: Officials highlighted coastal soil salinity, labour shortages due to urban migration, and delays in micro-irrigation implementation caused by staffing shortages in the horticulture department.

Agriculture & Irrigation: High groundwater salinity makes the region heavily dependent on canal irrigation, creating an urgent need to modernize the ageing canal network and improve irrigation infrastructure.

Fisheries & Aquaculture: Growth opportunities include establishing a marine lighthouse, strengthening fisheries infrastructure, expanding processing and market facilities for small-scale aquaculture farmers, and leveraging the new government crab hatchery for value addition and exports.
Animal Husbandry: Officials proposed introducing livestock insurance to reduce farmers' risks and improve resilience.

Traditional Industries: Strengthening market linkages for the Kalamkari artisan sector and establishing local manufacturing units for Machilipatnam's gold-covering industry were identified as priorities to reduce input costs and enhance competitiveness.

Infrastructure & Industrial Development: Investments in irrigation, fisheries infrastructure, processing facilities, and local manufacturing were identified as key drivers for improving productivity, reducing costs, and accelerating economic growth.

points: The district profiling session at NTR District was conducted in two batches to ensure focused engagement. Below are the key highlights: District Profiling ● The session began with a comprehensive profiling of NTR District, identifying its core strengths — agricultural and horticultural potential, Vijayawada's role as a major transport and commercial hub, a strong industrial base anchored by JLN Auto Nagar and Kondapalli Industrial Estate, and rich tourism and cultural heritage. ● Key challenges to be addressed were also discussed, including workforce skill gaps, limited access to modern technology in agriculture and industry, and over-reliance on traditional crops such as paddy, cotton, and mangoes. ● Officers engaged actively in mapping sectoral opportunities, including wholesale market hub development, food processing units for chillies and mangoes, eco-friendly aqua tourism around Bhavani Island, and cluster development for micro and small enterprises. Batch-wise Sessions ● The morning session brought together officers from agriculture and industry departments, who provided field-level inputs on crop diversification, value chain gaps, and industrial growth potential in the district. ● The afternoon session focused on service sector officers, covering education, health, tourism, transport, and welfare departments, with discussions on linking service delivery to district economic goals. Interactive Engagement ● Officers raised insightful questions and shared practical field-level experiences, making the training a two-way learning process. ● The trainers actively took inputs from the participants on ground realities, departmental data availability, and district-specific priorities to enrich the profiling exercise. ● The session on GDP and GVA measurement received an encouraging response, with officers showing keen interest in understanding how economic data supports evidence-based planning under the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 framework.

points: The district profiling session day 2 at NTR District was conducted to ensure focused engagement. Below are the key highlights: District Profiling ● The session began with a comprehensive brief of NTR District, explaining its core strengths through the vision documents and other secondary literature. ● The Officers present engaged actively in mapping sectoral opportunities, and the lead bank manager interacted with the team members along with other interactions. ● The lead bank officer gave his inputs on improving the credit access and prioritizing lending to the services and secondary sector as Amravati as a capital is emerging. The district also has ideas to introduce potential linked credit plans for better focused distribution. ● The key growth constraints mentioned was the competition from fintech and large banks and also the operational and technological gaps that are present in the banking sector. ● The team was mainly engaged in the analysis and making of the Woop framework and the district presentation of the NTR district.

coverage: As part of Day 3 of the Capacity Building Programme, the Constituency Profiling Exercise covered the Vijayawada East, Vijayawada Central, Vijayawada West, and Mylavaram constituencies. The Pahle India Foundation (PIF) team interacted with constituency- and mandal-level officials in online mode from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, opening each session with a briefing on the importance of ground-level inputs and how these feed into the Constituency Gross Value Added (CGVA) and Mandal Gross Value Added (MGVA) computation under the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 vision. Officials were also walked through the objectives and importance of the overall profiling exercise.

highlights.head: Vijayawada East Constituency
points: ● Animal Husbandry inputs highlighted regular deworming and vaccination drives, organic melas, and Goseva initiatives, supported by PKCC-linked dairy loans and a 50% feed subsidy strengthening livestock-based livelihoods.

● Auto Nagar was identified as a key steel and medical trade hub, with officials flagging the need for technical/skill training for local youth to match industry requirements. ● Zone C proposals centred on setting up MSME and food-processing units to widen the local industrial base. ● Urban amenity and tourism proposals included a medical hub, start-up innovation centre, EV charging hubs, night bazaars, food courts, and tourism development around Gunadala and Moghalrajapuram.

highlights.head: Vijayawada Central Constituency
points: ● Urbanised, service-driven economy: like Vijayawada West, Central's growth is anchored in the Service and MSME sectors, with officials citing urban land parcels for manufacturing/food-processing units clearable through Single Desk approvals. ● Dairy and allied livestock activity emerged as a common urban livelihood lever across East, West and Central, with scope for sex-sorted semen adoption, backyard poultry, and subsidized feed to raise milk GVA. ● Tourism and civic-infrastructure upgrades — echoing themes from West and Mylavaram — were flagged as priority areas, including heritage assets and drinking-water/waste-management improvements.

highlights.head: Vijayawada West Constituency
points: ● Zero agricultural and horticultural footprint, with the economy driven by the Service and Wholesale Trade sector centred on the One Town Market and Vegetable Wholesale Market near VMC. ● Durga Temple anchors tourism (₹300 crore master plan under consideration), with Bhavani Island identified for leisure/adventure tourism and a proposed unified tourist circuit. ● Micro-industries in the Kabela area (plastic poly-bags, nuts and bolts) could be scaled through a proposed multi-storey MSME hub on 1.5 acres (₹15 crore). ● Animal husbandry and fisheries potential via sex-sorted semen technology and 1,750 hectares of river land for fish cultivation, though spatial constraints and Pollution Control Board restrictions limit dairy/poultry expansion within city limits.

highlights.head: Mylavaram Constituency
points: ● Horticulture powerhouse: Mango cultivation across 15,000-18,000 acres (Totapuri, Chinna Rasalu), held back by the absence of cold storage and ripening infrastructure, with value-addition/export units proposed for the Reddigudem/Mylavaram belt. ● Floriculture and emerging crops (1,000+ acres of Jasmine, Oil Palm, Dragon Fruit) show promise, though rainfed dependency and delayed canal water remain key irrigation constraints. ● Kondapalli Industrial Estate (plastics, pharma, food processing) is constrained by poor roads and the lack of a Centralized Effluent Treatment Plant; MSME park expansion from 6.5 to 20 acres has been proposed. ● Ibrahimpatnam tourism circuit (Krishna-Godavari Sangam, Butterfly Park) and Kondapalli Toys offer tourism/handicraft potential, while dairy gains from sex-sorted semen and a 50% feed subsidy, and fisheries need cold-storage support and ban-period relief.

coverage: As part of Day 4 of the Capacity Building Programme, the Constituency Profiling Exercise covered the Nandigama, Jaggayyapeta, and Tiruvuru constituencies. The Pahle India Foundation (PIF) team interacted with constituency- and mandal-level officials in online mode from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, opening each session with a briefing on the importance of ground-level inputs and how these feed into the Constituency Gross Value Added (CGVA) and Mandal Gross Value Added (MGVA) computation under the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 vision.

highlights.head: Nandigama Constituency
points: ● Agriculture, horticulture and irrigation: Paddy and Cotton dominate, with a horticulture diversification push targeting 2,500 acres for conversion to Mango, Moringa and Nimbu under NREGS, alongside proposed lift-irrigation schemes and the long- pending Damuluru-Vaikuntapuram Bridge-cum-Barrage to link 28 lift irrigations and supply water to Amaravati. ● Animal husbandry and dairy: a transition to productive animals via sex-sorted semen supply is underway, backed by ~12,770 buffaloes as the major milch base and running milk-chilling units, though organized slaughterhouses and wild-cow crop damage along riverfronts remain unresolved challenges. ● Manufacturing, MSME and logistics: anchored by the Peddavaram APIIC Industrial Estate, Amba Coach, two operational ethanol plants and a completed Reliance CBG plant; 865 registered MSME units exist, but estate development remains poor and a dedicated MSME park is yet to be identified, with a Dry Port proposed at Kanchikacherla. ● Fisheries and tourism: 10 active fisheries societies and 19 minor irrigation tanks support ornamental-fisheries proposals, while a religious tourism circuit (Pallagiri Venkateswara Swamy - Gudimetla Sivalayam - Paritala Anjaneya Swamy) and growing farmhouse tourism in Kanchikacherla add to the proposed Auto Nagar expansion into a satellite city.

highlights.head: Jaggayyapeta Constituency
points: ● Agriculture and crop diversification: Paddy (10,300 acres), Cotton and Chilli (6,000 acres each) form the base, with a push for Oil Palm cultivation, vegetable exports to Hyderabad, and high-value horticulture (dragon fruit, avocado, apple ber) under 50% subsidy schemes. ● Food processing, MSME and industry: dedicated Chilli and Maize processing units are needed to capture local value, while the existing cement-unit base at S.N. Peta offers scope for ancillary/fabrication units and an emerging automobile industry opportunity supported by youth skilling programs. ● Tourism and pilgrimage: a dedicated circuit linking Vedadri - Tirumalagiri - Mutyala - Penuganchiprolu Ammavari Temple is proposed, with APSRTC-driven promotion and targeted last-mile pilgrim-road connectivity improvements. ● Animal husbandry and fisheries: a large livestock base (22,508 black cattle, 58,865 sheep, 15,905 goats) needs medium slaughterhouses (400-500 animal capacity), while 11 MI tanks, 13 societies and 470 licenses point to fisheries potential in ornamental fish culture, RAS and captive seed nurseries.

highlights.head: Tiruvuru Constituency

points: The district profiling session at Guntur District focused on the primary sector, with officers presenting departmental data on strengths, weaknesses, GVA contribution, ongoing schemes, and export/upcoming project potential. Below are the key highlights: District Profiling

The session began with a comprehensive profiling of Guntur District, identifying its core strengths — Animal Husbandry's 5.15% contribution to primary-sector GVA supported by breed upgradation and Pashu Kisan Credit Cards, and an established cold storage and market network supporting Fisheries and Agriculture produce movement.

Key challenges discussed included rising cultivation costs against stagnant MSP prices, near-total absence of active Farmer Producer Organizations despite high agricultural production, low Fisheries GVA contribution (1.2%) due to lack of cold storage and godown facilities, shrinking fodder land from urbanization, and insurance coverage limited to mortality only, not injuries

Officers engaged actively in mapping sectoral opportunities, including reviving FPOs for better market linkages, expanding PMMSY-backed subsidized transport support for fisheries, strengthening breed upgradation and insurance coverage under Animal Husbandry, and promoting forest awareness programs like Seed Balls and terrace greens to build student engagement despite forest cover being limited to just 5% of the district.

points: The district profiling session in Guntur District focused on the Industry and Service Sectors, with officials presenting departmental data on existing strengths, implementation challenges, ongoing initiatives, and opportunities to increase employment and GVA. Below are the key highlights: District Profiling ● The session highlighted major infrastructure and service-sector strengths, including substantial investments in urban water infrastructure, an extensive banking network of 539 branches and 123 CSP/BC outlets, and opportunities across industries, livelihoods, education, tourism, and other service sectors to support employment and economic growth. ● Key challenges discussed included delays in infrastructure execution due to inter-departmental clearances and financial processing, gaps in last-mile credit delivery to women, SC/ST, and PwD entrepreneurs, operational difficulties faced by CSPs, and the need for stronger coordination between education, skill development, enterprise, and employment opportunities. ● Officers actively explored sectoral opportunities for enhancing GVA and employment, including strengthening MSMEs and micro- enterprises, expanding institutional credit and SHG-linked entrepreneurship, improving urban infrastructure and service delivery, and developing tourism initiatives such as the Mirchi Festival, Tomato Games, temple tourism, and eco-tourism to generate local economic activity and livelihoods. points: Mandal-level officials from all three constituencies presented departmental inputs on existing strengths, challenges, and growth opportunities. Below are the key highlights: Tadikonda Constituency ● Horticulture and agriculture anchor the local economy, with chilli cultivation across ~5,000 Ha alongside cotton (4,200 Ha), turmeric, oil palm, and vegetables across Tadikonda, Thulluru, Medikonduru, and Firangipuram mandals. ● Officials flagged pesticide residue levels affecting EU/China chilli export compliance, a high tenant-farming ratio (~80%) limiting credit access, and water shortages from over-reliance on Nagarjuna Sagar Project canals. ● Animal husbandry shows strong scale with over 98,000 buffaloes across Tadikonda and Thulluru, presenting opportunities for milk-chilling units and dairy cooperatives, though feed shortages and low insurance coverage remain concerns. ● Infrastructure gaps discussed included ~1,200 pending Jal Jeevan Mission tap connections and the need for additional power lines to support stable 24/7 agricultural feeders. Mangalagiri Constituency ● The session covered GVA awareness and departmental coordination across Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, RWS, Irrigation, and Electricity for Mangalagiri, Tadepalli, and Duggirala mandals. ● Horticulture highlighted banana (~650 Ha) and turmeric (~400 Ha) as major crops, with proposals for banana chips/powder units, jasmine oil extraction, and a 30-metric-ton cold storage facility. ● Agriculture discussions centered on paddy and maize, with farmer requests for subsidized zinc/gypsum and irrigation motors, alongside drainage concerns raised in Nuthakki. ● RWS and Irrigation officials flagged a ₹135 crore CC drains proposal for Duggirala, pending JJM connections for 7,551 households, and modernization needs for the Guntur Channel (₹369 crore, at tender stage). Tenali Constituency ● Agriculture across Tenali and Kollipara spans 13,261 Ha of paddy along with Acid Lime and Banana; a 200 Ha sowing gap in Kollipara was linked to El Niño-driven water scarcity.

● Horticulture (1,635 Ha) is led by Turmeric, Banana, and Acid Lime, with only one 10-ton cold room serving the cluster — officials proposed 10-15 additional cold rooms and ripening chambers. ● Animal husbandry recorded a livestock and poultry population of ~77,000, with priorities including expanded sex-sorted semen use, cattle sheds for 40 members, and 90%-subsidized livestock insurance. ● Irrigation and utilities discussions covered a need for 140 radar/soil-moisture sensors, canal encroachments, 4 non-functional RO plants, and re-enrollment drives for around 1,200 untracked school dropouts.

coverage: The program covered online constituency profiling for the Guntur East, Guntur West, Prathipadu, and Ponnur constituencies, with mandal-level officials presenting sector-wise data on the Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, and allied infrastructure departments. Discussions focused on Gross Value Addition (GVA) potential, sectoral strengths, field-level challenges, and priority interventions to support evidence-based constituency planning.

points: Mandal-level officials from all three constituencies presented departmental inputs on existing strengths, challenges, and growth opportunities. Below are the key highlights: Ponnur Constituency ● Agriculture across Ponnur, Chebrole, and Pedakakani includes ~13,000 acres of Kharif paddy and 4,105 acres of Rabi crops including black gram, green gram, and maize, supported by the High-Level and Guntur Canal networks. ● Officials highlighted natural-calamity risks, shortages of subsidized tarpaulin sheets and modern sprayers, and the need for greater farm mechanization and canal desilting. ● Animal husbandry has strong potential with ~31,800 buffaloes, 20,100 sheep and goats, and 87,000 backyard poultry, though low insurance coverage, fodder shortages, and veterinary staff gaps remain concerns. ● Infrastructure and human-development gaps include 70 pending/in-progress JJM projects, 400 untraced school dropouts, lack of digital learning infrastructure, and 64 acres of irrigation land encroachments in Chebrole. Guntur East Constituency ● Guntur East functions as an industrial, logistics, and agro-processing hub with no significant crop cultivation, supported by 125 cold-storage units, Sortex chilli grading, spice-processing units, solar dryers, ripening chambers, and refrigerated transport. ● Animal husbandry focuses on dairy and pet animals with vaccination and mobile veterinary services, while high feed costs remain a concern; fisheries activity is organized through Fishermen and Women Cooperative Societies rather than aquaculture or natural fishing. ● Education covers 45 Primary and High Schools, with student welfare support and specialized services for children with disabilities, though dropout surveys are ongoing and slow backend servers affect administration. ● Infrastructure gaps include summer peak-load electricity disruptions, limited processing subsidies for small-scale chilli/pickle units, and the need for stronger financial support and banker engagement for agro-processing enterprises.

highlights.head: Guntur west Constituency
points: ● Guntur West is a highly urbanized economy with no significant agricultural activity, driven primarily by real estate, hospitality, healthcare, commercial services, and CRDA infrastructure works. ● Education includes 119 government schools, with welfare benefits and Mid-Day Meals fully provided, while reported dropout figures are being reassessed due to migration and demographic factors. ● Solid-waste management includes dry/wet waste segregation, vermicomposting, and reuse of shredded plastic and glass in BT roads, though source segregation and public awareness require improvement. ● Key operational gaps include high livestock feed costs, staff shortages affecting electricity KPI tracking, and the need for stronger urban waste-management awareness.Irrigation and utilities discussions covered a need for 140 radar/soil-moisture sensors, canal encroachments, 4 non-functional RO plants, and re-enrollment drives for around 1,200 untracked school dropouts. Prathipadu Constituency

Horticulture across Pedanandipadu, Vatticherukuru, Prathipadu, and Kakumanu is dominated by red chilli, while agriculture is centered on cotton, paddy, chilli, and Bengal gram; delayed rainfall has affected sowing and canal- dependent irrigation.

Officials flagged chilli viral diseases and pest attacks, heavy fertilizer use, wild-pig damage, and inadequate storage/drying facilities, with farmers seeking virus-resistant varieties, subsidized tarpaulin sheets, godowns, and custom-hiring harvesters.

Animal husbandry is largely small- and medium-scale, with backyard poultry promoted among women; fodder scarcity and an unorganized dairy sector remain concerns, creating scope for value-addition training and organized dairy farming.

Infrastructure and service gaps include water scarcity in parts of Prathipadu and Vatticherukuru, delayed filter replacement, pollution around irrigation tanks, 19 irrigation staff vacancies, and understaffing across RWS and Gram Panchayat offices

sessions.format: One-to-one interactions 2nd – 3rd July – District Profiling The discussions focused on the current status of each sector, key strengths, challenges, ongoing interventions, and future development opportunities.

highlights.head: Method                 One-to-one interactions
points: The discussions focused on the current status of each sector, key strengths, challenges, ongoing interventions, and future development opportunities. Key Findings › Agriculture: Shift focus from productivity gains to crop diversification, integrated farming (paddy–fish culture), expansion of cultivable area, and reducing cultivation costs to improve farmer incomes. Strengthen food processing, cold storage, and agricultural value chains.

Horticulture: Promote acid lime, mango, papaya, and floriculture through improved post-harvest infrastructure, packhouses, value addition, and climate-resilient orchard management to enhance export and market potential.
Animal Husbandry: Expand milk, meat, and egg production by strengthening breed improvement, veterinary services, fodder development, and livestock productivity enhancement programmes.
Fisheries: Leverage 42,000 acres of aquaculture and the sector’s 12% contribution to district GVA by expanding inland and marine aquaculture, processing facilities, and seafood value addition.
Forestry: Promote sustainable forestry, biodiversity conservation, and eco-restoration while creating livelihood opportunities through forest-based activities.

Industry: Unlock growth through mineral resource development, MSME expansion, industrial value addition, manufacturing growth, and construction sector development, supported by future mineral exploration.
Tourism & Services: Position Mypadu Beach and other coastal attractions as tourism hubs by integrating culture, heritage, and local cuisine while strengthening tourism data systems.

Human Capital & Infrastructure: Improve healthcare infrastructure, skill development, education quality, road connectivity, drinking water supply, and public infrastructure to support long-term economic growth and service delivery.
4th July – Constituency Profiling (4 Constituencies)

Atmakur Constituency: Growth can be driven by strengthening paddy, tobacco, Bengal gram, and cotton cultivation while expanding banana and mango horticulture. Investments in cold storage, food processing units, MSME parks, and spiritual tourism infrastructure can significantly enhance value addition and GVA.

Sarvepalli Constituency: The constituency has strong potential in paddy, lemon cultivation, aquaculture, mango, and organic farming. Leveraging the Adani Krishnapatnam Port, expanding oil palm cultivation, strengthening FPOs, improving livestock productivity, and developing post-harvest infrastructure can accelerate economic growth.

Kovuru Constituency: Growth opportunities lie in paddy, groundnut, sericulture, jasmine cultivation, aquaculture (15,000 acres), and horticulture in Indukurpet Mandal. Strengthening cold storage, value addition, and market linkages will improve farmer incomes and sectoral GVA.

Kavali Constituency: The constituency has strong prospects in paddy, fisheries, mango (3,200 acres), and acid lime cultivation. Investments in fish processing units, cold chain infrastructure, fishermen insurance, tourism development, and water resource management can unlock significant growth potential. Common Priorities: Across all four constituencies, officials highlighted the need for post-harvest infrastructure, food processing, market connectivity, value addition, tourism promotion, and sector-specific interventions to improve productivity, create employment, and enhance Gross Value Added (GVA) under Swarna Andhra Vision 2047.

coverage: As part of the Constituency-Level Capacity Building Programme, two sessions were conducted today: Gudur Constituency in the morning and Sarvepalli Constituency in the evening. Both sessions focused on strengthening the understanding of Mandal-level officers on Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross Value Added (GVA), and constituency-level economic planning under the Swarna Andhra Pradesh @2047 Vision.

highlights.head: Gudur Constituency
points: The programme commenced with a welcome and introduction of the PIF team by the Young Professional (YP). Despite many officers being engaged in other official responsibilities such as the SIR programme, most Mandal-level officers attended the session and actively participated.

The team then presented the constituency's economic profile, highlighting that the primary sector is the major contributor, with fisheries and aquaculture playing a dominant role due to Gudur's long coastal belt. Throughout the presentation, the PIF team encouraged interaction with the officers to validate the data and obtain field-level insights. Officers from various departments provided valuable suggestions and practical interventions based on local realities.

Sector-wise discussions were also held to identify development opportunities. In the primary sector, officers emphasized the need for improved irrigation facilities and better water management systems to enhance agricultural productivity. Similar discussions were held for the secondary and tertiary sectors to identify growth interventions. In the health sector, officers highlighted the need to upgrade the Chinthavaram Primary Health Centre (PHC) into a Community Health Centre (CHC) to improve healthcare accessibility. The session concluded with a case study demonstrating successful constituency-level development practices.

highlights.head: Sarvepalli Constituency
points: The evening session was conducted at Sarvepalli Constituency, where the Young Professional and CVAP Unit extended excellent hospitality and formally introduced the PIF team. The programme followed a similar structure, beginning with the importance of the Capacity Building Programme, followed by the methodology of GDP and GVA estimation, and finally the constituency-level economic analysis.

A notable aspect of this session was the active participation of representatives from the MLA's office, who sought suggestions and interventions from the PIF team for the overall development of the constituency. This reflected the strong interest in evidence-based planning and constituency development.

The discussions highlighted several strengths of the constituency. Officers informed that around 11 palm oil processing units are functioning in the constituency, generating employment while simultaneously encouraging oil palm cultivation, thereby contributing to the growth of the primary sector. In addition, the constituency has more than 6,000 MSMEs, which significantly contribute to employment generation and industrial development.

Departmental officers also shared several practical suggestions. In the primary sector, they recommended promoting green fodder cultivation to reduce livestock feeding costs. Although various industries operate within the constituency, officers pointed out that local youth often do not secure employment or internships due to a lack of career guidance after completing skill development programmes. They emphasized that while skill training is available, stronger post-training support and employment linkage mechanisms are needed.

Another important suggestion was the productive utilization of unused government lands. Officers proposed promoting forestry or encouraging local communities to undertake plantation and other productive activities on these lands, with the income generated being utilized for Panchayat development and local infrastructure improvement.

Both sessions witnessed active participation and meaningful discussions, with officers contributing valuable field-level insights and practical interventions. The interactions will be useful in refining constituency-level Vision Action Plans and promoting evidence-based planning for sustainable and inclusive development.

coverage: The Capacity Building Training Programme on GDDP/GMDP for Kurnool district was conducted on 18 July 2026 through in- person departmental interaction sessions. A four-member team engaged district officials across Primary, Secondary and Tertiary sector departments to capture sector-wise field observations, ongoing programmes, implementation status, systemic constraints and key recommendations, in line with the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 District Economic Profiling framework.

highlights.head: Primary Sector
points: Agriculture and horticulture (cotton, red gram, groundnut, chilli, onion, tomato, mango and other crops) remain the mainstay of the district economy, constrained above all by water scarcity, a nearly two-year delay in micro-irrigation subsidy disbursement, and weak processing, drying and cold-storage infrastructure across crops.

Livestock and fisheries show good production potential (milk, meat, eggs; Catla/Rohu/Mrigal across ~246 tanks and four reservoirs) but need stronger veterinary infrastructure, breed improvement, hatchery modernisation and reduced tank siltation to translate into higher value addition.

Forest and Housing departments both face resourcing pressure: encroachment and mining threaten roughly 40,000– 50,000 ha of forest cover, while long-pending housing subsidy grievances persist even as new project sites are identified at Peddapadu and Orvakal.

highlights.head: Secondary Sector
points: Kurnool's location on NH-44 and the ~10,000-acre Orvakal Industrial Corridor (chemical, food-processing, textile, defence, IT and Drone City proposals) position the district well for industrial growth, though water availability and additional power infrastructure remain key constraints.

The district is emerging as a major renewable-energy hub, with 664 MW of solar and 830 MW of wind already installed and ~7,121 MW sanctioned, but limited government land and weak PPA access for smaller developers constrain further expansion.

Mineral resources (road metal, quartz, granite, sand) remain underexploited because of financial constraints, lease regulations that treat 1-acre and 100-acre leases alike, and a shortage of technical staff for exploration and monitoring.

highlights.head: Tertiary Sector
points: Urban infrastructure programmes (AMRUT, Legacy Waste Management, Municipal Corporation civic works) are progressing but routinely take far longer than planned because of land acquisition, encroachments and contractor delays, leaving drinking water and sanitation as persistent urban gaps.

Tourism has substantial untapped potential, with ₹14 crore in new proposals (Ramjal Lake, Ashoka Shila Sasanam, a Jain Temple and others) and several heritage sites awaiting funding, while banking and revenue services need improved credit access for lease farmers and MSMEs.

Employment & Skill Development runs active job melas and multiple national schemes (PMKVY, DDU-GKY, NCS), but only ~20% of registrants secure employment, and new industrial investors have yet to share specific skilling requirements, limiting future-ready training design.

coverage: The Capacity Building Training Programme on GDDP/GCDP/GMDP for Kurnool district was conducted on 20 July 2026 as a full-day, highly interactive in-person session under the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 initiative, delivered by the Pahle India Foundation (PIF) to District HODs, CSOs and MSOs. The session was opened by CPO Smt. G. Bharathi, who invited District Collector Dr. A. Siri to formally inaugurate the programme. Mr. Harshavardhan of PIF then introduced the purpose of the session and briefed participants on PIF's mandate, followed by a session on the Swarna Andhra @

2047 vision and mission for 2047. Dr. Subramaniam took participants through GDP and economic indicators, followed by a session on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and how to monitor them at the district level. After a short break, Mr. Harshavardhan spoke on strategies to boost sectoral Gross Value Added (GVA), following which Ms. Havila presented the Kurnool district profile, highlighting its key strengths and opportunities. Mr. Harshavardhan then presented two case studies — the Sahyadri Farms food processing model and the Baramati agrotourism model — to illustrate replicable approaches for the district. The session concluded with closing remarks by CPO Smt. G. Bharathi. District Collector Dr. A. Siri remained present for the entire duration of the session, from the morning inauguration through to the closing remarks in the evening.

points: The session ran the full scheduled duration, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and was noted as highly interactive throughout.
District Collector Dr. A. Siri was present for the entire session, from the morning to the evening, reflecting strong district-level ownership of the programme.

Improving Horticulture GVA under Rainfed Conditions: Participants asked how horticulture GVA could be improved given that most cultivation in the district is rainfed. Experts responded with examples of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) as a model to strengthen aggregation, market linkages and value addition.

Addressing Migration: A second query concerned migration, flagged as one of the district's major weaknesses. Experts recommended a focus on agrotourism and farm-stay models, citing case studies from Punjab and Sri Lanka, as a means of generating local income and reducing outward migration from Kurnool.

coverage: The exercise consolidated structured consistuency level profiling across Alur, Mantryalayam, Panyam, and Pattikonda, capturing field- level evidence on village-level growth patterns and success factors, employment and livelihood shifts, sectoral contribution to economic growth, statistical data gaps and reporting bottlenecks, land use and land disputes, tenant farming, drought vulnerability, livestock and dairy development, and the reach of animal husbandry and other government programmes, to support evidence-based constituency planning under Swarna Andhra @ 2047.

highlights.head: Pattikonda
points: Growth is increasingly transport- and service-led, concentrated along the NH-44 corridor and around Pattikonda town, driven by irrigation infrastructure, road connectivity, residential and commercial expansion, and improved education, health and government-scheme delivery, even as agricultural land near the town steadily converts to residential and commercial use.

Employment is visibly shifting away from agriculture toward construction, transport, retail/services, small-scale industry and self- employment, accompanied by rising seasonal and permanent migration and an ageing farm workforce in remoter villages.

Statistical systems struggle to capture tenant cultivation, seasonal migration, informal employment and household income, compounded by outdated land-use/household records and duplicate-entry, connectivity and staffing gaps at the Village Secretariat, while chronic drought exposure is only partly addressed by schemes such as Pathu Bharosa, PM-KISAN and MGNREGS.

highlights.head: Alur
points: Livestock anchors Tuggali's economy - roughly 15,000 cattle, 85,000 sheep/goats and 15,000 poultry (approx.) - with sheep and goat rearing, especially among landless SC/ST communities, forming a major livelihood base alongside limited dairy income where irrigation supports fodder production.

Animal husbandry service delivery is strong: Artificial Insemination under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (including sex-sorted semen) covers 60-70% of livestock farmers, FMD/Brucellosis vaccination coverage stands at 100% with no recent outbreaks, and the 1962 Mobile Veterinary Clinic reaches remote villages within roughly 30-60 minutes of a farmer's request.

Growth is concentrated around Tuggali village/mandal headquarters and gold-mining-driven Jonnagiri, alongside a shift to drought- tolerant crops and rising land prices; the mandal remains chronically drought-prone, with declining groundwater, encroached grazing/tank lands and continued migration despite MGNREGS, PMAY and SHG programmes.

highlights.head: Panyam
points: Agriculture continues to be the primary source of livelihood, but there is a clear shift towards employment in renewable energy, industries, trade, transport, and other service-sector activities, creating more diversified income opportunities for rural households.

Although basic infrastructure has improved across most villages, significant gaps remain in drainage systems, internal roads, solid and liquid waste management, and sanitation facilities, which continue to affect the quality of life and economic development.

Agricultural modernization through mechanization, improved irrigation practices, adoption of commercial crops, and better market access has significantly enhanced farm productivity and contributed to higher rural incomes. •

highlights.head: Mantralayam
points: Red chilli and onion cultivation has expanded rapidly because these crops offer better market prices, higher profitability, and are well suited to the local climatic conditions.

The major constraint to horticulture development is the lack of assured year-round irrigation, which limits the adoption of water- intensive crops and reduces the expansion of schemes such as oil palm cultivation.

Farmers continue to face significant post-harvest and marketing challenges due to inadequate cold storage, packhouses, and processing facilities, resulting in crop losses and dependence on middlemen for selling their produce.

coverage: The District Master Training under the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 Capacity Building Programme was conducted as a full-day, in-person programme from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM at Horticulture Bhavan, Kurnool. The programme brought together master trainers and field-level officers from all mandals of Kurnool district to develop a shared understanding of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross Value Added (GVA), sectoral growth drivers, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and their role in cascading the training to field-level functionaries. The programme commenced with inaugural remarks by the Chief Planning Officer (CPO), who emphasized the importance of the initiative and encouraged participants to remain focused on the programme objectives while ensuring effective implementation at the grassroots level. The Deputy Statistical Officer (DSO) also addressed the gathering, and the Director of the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES) attended the programme, highlighting the significance of the capacity-building initiative. The first technical session was delivered by Mr. Krishna, who provided an overview of the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 Mission. The session outlined the vision, strategic priorities, and the role of district administrations in achieving the state's long-term development goals. This was followed by a comprehensive technical session led by Mr. Rahees on GDP and GVA. The session explained the conceptual differences between GDP and GVA, their significance in measuring economic performance, and the methodologies used for their estimation. The concepts were reinforced through interactive discussions and practical exercises using real-world examples. Participants actively engaged in numerical exercises to strengthen their understanding of GDP and GVA estimation. Building on these concepts, the session focused on identifying opportunities to enhance Kurnool district's Gross Value Added (GVA). A detailed sector-wise discussion was conducted using district-specific examples from agriculture, industry, and services to analyse existing strengths, identify growth constraints, and explore strategies for improving economic performance. The discussion enabled participants to relate theoretical concepts to practical planning and highlighted the importance of targeted sectoral interventions in driving sustainable district-level economic growth.

points: Explained the concepts of GDP and GVA, their importance, and the basic methods used to calculate them.
Discussed the major sectors contributing to Kurnool district's economy and identified opportunities to increase GVA.
Introduced Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and explained how they can be used to monitor sectoral performance and economic growth.
Emphasized the role of master trainers in conducting similar training programmes for field-level officials and supporting effective implementation at the grassroots level
Training already concluded in districts of Parvathipuram Manyam and Chittoor
